Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Act 1 Overview
Honestly, the main skills we are pretty similar between Acts 1 and 2, as well as gear priority.
For the vast majority of the run, we'll be using  to clear groups that are primed for stun, and even as a potent single-target nuke when empowered with ; it can hit deceptively hard on a boss when socketed with  and .
I kid you not,  (and even its single-wielded counterpart) is one of your best DPS abilities, and is usually what I'm spamming to buildup Stun or dealing DPS during heavy stun windows. We also have  and  socketed for even more damage.
 is something we get towards the end of the Act, and it is a potent stun-primer as well as a good way to break armour on targets. You definitely want to keep up the Fully Broken Armour debuff on bosses, and tapping this every now and then is an easy way to do that.
But, since we get that skill towards the end of the Act, the most important things to keep up to date are your Maces. Check the vendors frequently for good maces as that's what's going to deal the vast majority of your damage in this Act. 
A high armour Shield is just a "bonus" at this point, though it will make your s, , and even your Shield Bashes from  hit a lot harder and buildup more stun.
QUICK NOTE: I think that, with  becoming a Tier 1 support gem, 's Shield Bash will become the best way to Prime targets for Stun early on in your playthrough, and potentially onwards. It doesn't take much to block attacks and Shield Bash, then follow up with a ; just means you may invest into some Stun Threshold and socket  with . 
I genuinely think this will be the best way to clear with  as a Shield Warrior, and potentially any Warrior.
As far as Runeshaping goes in 0.5, prioritize getting extra Support Gems to crank up your skills, Body runes for a bit of extra life, and try to grab a Storm Rune at some point so we have an assured way to deal Lightning Damage as we upgrade our Maces from tier-to-tier (this is so we can inflict the Shock ailment while DPSing with ; I usually save it for an Act 2 Mace)

Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Act 2 Overview
Overall things are similar to Act 1 when it comes to clearing; we're now priming things for stun using , and slapping them with our dual-wielded . This still feels great for clearing, and depending on how high of an armour value Shield you have, you can prime groups for stun in 1-2  taps (especially now that we have access to the  support gem).
Aside from that, we eventually do get access to  in this Act, but we only really have on reliable "detonator" for it: , and this has a hefty cooldown in its current form. So you can choose to throw these down during boss fights for a quick hit but honestly, I find that leaning into the maces is still the right call here. 
You could go for some Endurance Charge generation via  and support gems like  to bypass the  cooldown, but I just found leaning into the Mace damage was still easier and less complicated to setup for the majority of this Act.  still goes hard for boss damage.
IMPORTANT NOTE:  is a much stronger option early on if you decide to go Warbringer, then respec your Ascendancy to Smith of Kitava in the endgame. I'm just catering this build for those of you who don't want to have to respec later on, though I will say that Warbringer is the faster leveler, with the no-cooldown Warshouts and exploding corpses from them to clear.

Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Act 3 Overview
We get access to  here, which is now what we want to detonate our Shield Walls with; we still use  as well, but we use this before we slam down our s so that they are empowered. It's a strong combo, but one that I pretty much exclusively use in boss fights, or on a stubborn Rare.
Clearing, honestly, still looks the same with priming things for stun with  or  and then chaining s. This means we should be keeping our Maces up-to-date frequently, as always.
That said, don't neglect your Shield quite as much anymore; we want to use  +   +  to delete bosses once you get a high-roll armour Shield, and even  can do some strong deleting on its own when clearing.
As far as the Trial of Chaos is concerned... honestly you could just skip it for now. I feel like the benefit of using a Normal quality body chestpiece for only two of the  bonuses may not be worth it over a decent Rare during this Act, so you can wait until later when you'd also get your 5th and 6th Ascendancy points in a higher level Trial.

Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Act 4 Overview
This is the Act where we finally start transitioning into . I would not recommend taking this until you've allocated  on the Passive Skill Tree, which we've been pathing to since the previous Act. Once you get this, your Fully Broken Armour effects will apply to your Fire Damage, which is a 20% increased damage bonus at minimum. This helps offset the 25% damage that goes "missing" once you take , and makes that downside feel less terrible.
I'd also recommend having a +% increased elemental damage roll on a weapon you've found before the change as well.
We're still using  to clear quite a bit, however it's sometime during this act that I toss the dual-wielded Maces portion of this build so that I can lock-in a strong, high-armour Shield for Weapon Set 2 points, which will start cranking up our Ignite damage on bosses. Make sure  is no longer set to Weapon Set 2, and you should be hitting hard enough for it to feel good clearing in the latter part of this Act.
Gearing and Support Gems take a bit of a turn as well since we can now benefit from various increased Fire Damage and Elemental Damage rolls.
One last note, there is a Kalguuran Skill Gem called  that can seemingly be VERY strong if you can time the Parry-window right; that's 50% more damage during a potential boss punish window. It's a little hard to line up, but definitely worth the try and is the best one out of the choices you can pick in this Act.

Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Interludes Overview
Largely similar to Act 4, but we're now starting to fully-invest into the Fire and Ignite theme for boss-killing. Honestly, clearing with  still works well for much of the interludes, and is what I'd recommend until we're closer to Early Mapping and can path to  around level 70ish for a big AoE increase.
Pay close attention to gearing in this Act as we want to make sure we're maintaining a decent level of Fire Resistance to keep ourselves resist-capped, even though we'll likely be buying a few cheap items to take care of Chaos Resist cap as we head into maps.
A high armour Shield is important as always, as well as a decent mace with +melee skills and % increased elemental damage; check vendors often for options.
Monsters that happen to roll high Fire Resistance can be stubborn, but not terribly so; Shield Wall will still hit very hard and inflict exposure through , which helps cut through the Resistances a little bit. Still, they can be annoying until we get access to the  support gem, which we'll socket in every hard-hitting skill we have (obviously replace  in  once you get these).

Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Early Maps Overview
Early maps are "fine," I would say for this build, but it's not until you get  and  that your clear starts becoming VERY strong. For now, standard s will serve perfectly fine for clearing and bossing.
When clearing, go ahead and just spam  detonated with , simple as that. You can channel some  between s if you'd like as you are repositioning so that you can get some more Rage generation and stacks of armour for .
When bossing, fully break armour on the boss first with , make sure you are Rage-capped, then , , and , in that order. Repeat the last two if necessary but you'll be able to burn early map bosses down reasonably quickly with this setup.
If you are trade league, first thing you should do is grab a cheap set of armour with a bunch of +% Fire Resist to cap out your resistances, and try your best to cap out Chaos Resistance at 75% as well. It's not the end of the world if you aren't 75% since we have the useful  allocated in our Ascendancy, but I suggest trying to grab some Chaos Resistance on Belt, Helmet, and Boots for now if you are able.
SSF Players, obviously you are at the whim of what you find and craft, but similarly prioritize stacking Armour, Fire Resistance, and life where you can.

Lexd's Shield Wall + Avatar of Fire Smith of Kitava for 0.5.5: The Forbidden Rites

IMPORTANT NOTE: Everyone keeps asking me this so I'm going to make a note here at the top; the shield is set to both weapon sets (Mobalytics currently does not have the feature to display this), make sure you hover your mouse over the Roman Numerals above your Shield in your equipment screen and lock it to both sets!

Hey guys! This is the 
Smith of Kitava
 version of my classic 
Avatar of Fire
 Shield Warrior build that I've now made on every Ascendancy. Compared to the 
Titan
 and 
Warbringer
, this definitely felt the tankiest out of them all (especially on a budget), and has some really good sustain with 
Blood Magic
 since we can get so much life and life regen through this Ascendancy.

Previously, we we're using 
Fortifying Cry
 and 
Resonating Shield
 with some sizeable AoE boosts from our Passive Skill Tree as our main way to clear maps and other endgame activities. 

However, I've recently been using 
Shield Wall
 with the classic 
Ahn's Citadel
 and 
Kaom's Madness
 combo as my main way to clear since it just covers so much AoE and deals so much damage; you will simply have to optimize for more skill/attack speed for this method of clearing, which is apparent in the "0.5 Nebuloch + Avatar of Fire Optimized" tab below. The switch was necessary to make 200% Delirium and juiced Grand Expeditions doable, which we can now tackle with ease using this setup.

Aside from that, on bosses we have a bunch of Weapon Set 2 points to crank up our single-target and Ignite damage, so our 
Shield Wall
s will inflict significant Fire Damage over time when they are empowered with 
Infernal Cry
 and detonated with 
Fortifying Cry
. Yes, 
Fortifying Cry
 is still the best detonator for 
Shield Wall
 (check the note below). Just make sure that you have a full Rage Bar + the boss has been hit with 
Sunder
 recently, as the latter skill increases our Fire Damage by a whopping ~40% when inflicted before mods.

QUICK NOTE: this build was affected by the 
Fortifying Cry
 + 
Shield Wall
 shotgun nerf, but the damage of 
Shield Wall
 itself and the subsequent Ignites it inflicts are still significant. You will likely get more damage out of my Bleed build here, but this is still a solid option for taking down bosses and 
Fortifying Cry
 is still the ideal detonator for 
Shield Wall
 since it's just... well, an extra attack that scales with your shield's armour (which will be very high) which is also counted as an "Empowered Attack." It's still super strong.

As mentioned earlier, we are incredibly tanky thanks to Ascendancy nodes like 
Kitavan Engraving
, 
Leather Bindings
, 
Heatproofing
, 
Dedication to Kitava
, etc. There are a few options to go with here but those first three I think are must-haves for this build, especially early on in mapping.

That's basically it! I wish that Ignite was a bit of a stronger Ailment, but it is "serviceable" as a way to burn-down bosses, especially if they happen to leap away or become hard to hit.

There is now a  
Nebuloch
 that uses a combination of Critical Damage Bonus + Ignite Passive Skill Tree nodes and gear that inflicts some VERY strong Ignites. These used to be Chaos Damage Ignites that worked with 
Blackflame
 and stacking Wither through 
Withering Presence
, but GGG has since nerfed this interaction and we now just want to cut through Fire Resistances some other way. I go over a few different methods in this video.

Keep an eye out for 0.5.5 updates as I play through with this character; I think some of the new soul cores could be relevant to boosting the build!

Strengths and Weaknesses
Very tanky; one of the most durable builds I've played
Strong clear, can tackle all endgame activities with relative ease
Feels very "versatile," i.e. you can tailor the passive skill tree for different synergies considering the ascendancy (e.g. self-ignite, maximum resistances, etc.)
Budget-friendly; very easy to get Resist Capped and survivable with little currency spent
What we gain in a tankiness we sacrifice a little bit of damage for, but not a large amount
Fast enough, but not the most "zoomy"

Smith of Kitava + Avatar of Fire Shield Warrior: Act 1 Overview

Honestly, the main skills we are pretty similar between Acts 1 and 2, as well as gear priority.

For the vast majority of the run, we'll be using 
Boneshatter
 to clear groups that are primed for stun, and even as a potent single-target nuke when empowered with 
Infernal Cry
; it can hit deceptively hard on a boss when socketed with 
Impact Shockwave
 and 
Fire Attunement
.

I kid you not, 
Mace Strike
 (and even its single-wielded counterpart) is one of your best DPS abilities, and is usually what I'm spamming to buildup Stun or dealing DPS during heavy stun windows. We also have 
Rapid Attacks I
 and 
Rage I
 socketed for even more damage.

Resonating Shield
 is something we get towards the end of the Act, and it is a potent stun-primer as well as a good way to break armour on targets. You definitely want to keep up the Fully Broken Armour debuff on bosses, and tapping this every now and then is an easy way to do that.

But, since we get that skill towards the end of the Act, the most important things to keep up to date are your Maces. Check the vendors frequently for good maces as that's what's going to deal the vast majority of your damage in this Act. 

A high armour Shield is just a "bonus" at this point, though it will make your 
Shield Charge
s, 
Resonating Shield
, and even your Shield Bashes from 
Raise Shield
 hit a lot harder and buildup more stun.

QUICK NOTE: I think that, with 
Brink I
 becoming a Tier 1 support gem, 
Raise Shield
's Shield Bash will become the best way to Prime targets for Stun early on in your playthrough, and potentially onwards. It doesn't take much to block attacks and Shield Bash, then follow up with a 
Boneshatter
; just means you may invest into some Stun Threshold and socket 
Raise Shield
 with 
Steadfast I
. 

I genuinely think this will be the best way to clear with 
Boneshatter
 as a Shield Warrior, and potentially any Warrior.

As far as Runeshaping goes in 0.5, prioritize getting extra Support Gems to crank up your skills, Body runes for a bit of extra life, and try to grab a Storm Rune at some point so we have an assured way to deal Lightning Damage as we upgrade our Maces from tier-to-tier (this is so we can inflict the Shock ailment while DPSing with 
Mace Strike
; I usually save it for an Act 2 Mace)

Obviously don't go in naked with just your boots; just use whatever you can find for the blank spots, strong amour pieces, Rares you can wear, etc. 

I only put the most important pieces you should keep somewhat up-to-date in this Act. Keep an eye out for strong Maces and a Shield, with a much higher priority on Maces. I also included the most important rolls on each if you mouse over each item.

Boneshatter

Using two one-handed maces also takes advantage of how our Passive Skill Tree is setup, but we'll get more into that later; I cannot stress enough how much of a game-changer using Dual-Wielded maces was for me when it comes to damage, and you are still able to get a ton of use out of your Shield. Try it out.

Last note; try to get a Lightning Damage roll on one, and/or keep some Storm Runes in the bank to throw into some Maces with sockets later on. This let's us apply the Shock ailment on bosses as we're hitting them with
